mechanism: exact block-scalar identity in the qubit⊗Fock decomposition (centre of SU(2) per photon-number block); dirty-qubit catalyst

rule.name: kerr_half_pi_dirty_catalyst_triple_cr
rule.idea: Target exp(-i theta n^2) at theta == pi/2 (mod 2pi), or its mirror -pi/2. On each photon-number block n, the product W = CR_Z(pi).CR_X(pi).CR_Y(pi) of three qubit-controlled rotations acts on the qubit as (-iZ)^n(-iX)^n(-iY)^n = s(n)*I (period-4 sign pattern), exactly, for every n: W is the identity on the qubit for any qubit state, so no clean ancilla is needed -- the site qubit already co-located with the mode can be used as a dirty catalyst and returns unchanged. Multiplying by R(-pi/2) turns s(n) into exp(-i pi n^2/2) exactly, since n^2 mod 4 = n mod 2. CR_X/CR_Y are CR(pi) conjugated by H / S.H respectively. Y must be applied first in time, then X, then Z (order of the operator product matters). The mirrored theta = -pi/2 case is the Hermitian conjugate circuit: reverse the gate order, CR(pi) -> CR(-pi), swap s/sdg, and R(-pi/2) -> R(+pi/2).

reason: rule never chosen/applied on any benchmark
